releases.title: The North
releases.about:
# The North

Two pieces from Logic Moon that face away from the light. The North is not a place on a map, it is a direction of travel — and everything that way gets colder, thinner, quieter.

Spectre opens in half-light. Sustained tones that never quite resolve, something moving at the edge of hearing. The North follows it out into the open, where the air is thin enough to see through and the reverb runs longer than it should.

Ethereal, but not weightless. Something is underneath.

releases.title: Spelrum
releases.about:
# Spelrum

A collaboration between Logic Moon and Henrik Meierkord — two ambient practitioners meeting in the space between control and drift. "Spelrum" is Swedish for room to move, leeway, the margin left open for something to happen. That's the record: two players trading restraint for restraint, until what's left is the gap between them.

"Tidsmarginal" opens the EP as its emotional core — slow, aching tonal shifts measured against a clock that never quite resolves. "Spelrum" closes it under tension, low tones held taut rather than released, cello overtones bowing through the mix, the leeway of the title never fully cashed in.

Two tracks. No excess. The Moon Records at its coldest and most patient.

releases.title: Sub Lacuna
releases.about:
# Sub Lacuna

The new album from Aethery Fields is a journey into the damp, pressurised depths of the subconscious. Where earlier works drifted through foggy expanses, this album descends, slowly, irreversibly, through layers of sound that feel like water. Cold. Alive. Restless.
Turbulent textures meet organic stillness. Kelp forests sway in the shifting light of currents. The ocean floor breathes. Sub Lacuna is the most experimental work under the Aethery Fields banner to date, an album that sounds wet, in every sense of the word.
Tracks like Sub Lacuna, Kelp Reef Garden and Sea Floor are not merely locations. They are states of being. Levels of consciousness. Measures of pressure.
